To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have achieved 79% classification accuracy in CEFR level prediction using morphological features and POS tags, and we have shown that regression modeling is less effective than classification for this task.

(1) classification is more effective for this task than regression, (2) classification between groups is more effective than multiclass classification, (3) morphological features are the most predictive features and (4) features that are predictive of the CEFR level are also highly predictive of other features, such as the length of the text and the frequency of the most frequent word in the text.
the classification accuracy for the multiclass task is 0.79, for the binary task 0.81 and the correlation between the predicted and actual CEFR level for the regression task is 0,85.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic CEFR level prediction of learners’ texts in Estonian, a morphologically rich and agglutinative language.
automatic CEFR prediction of learners’ texts.
the development of a tool that could be used for automatic language assessment and for the evaluation of language learning materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
classification is a better method for the task of CEFR level prediction.
the classification model is more effective than the regression model in predicting the CEFR level of a learner.
classification is a more effective method for predicting CEFR levels of learners’ texts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully developed a system that is capable of automatically assessing a learner’s proficiency according to CEFR.
the most predictive features are the ones that reflect the learner’s knowledge of the language.
the most predictive features are the morphological and syntactical features of the learner texts and that the best approach is classification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphological features of the learner texts, especially the verb forms, are the most important predictors for language proficiency.
the automatic CEFR level prediction for Estonian learner texts is a feasible task.
the automatic prediction of CEFR levels for learner text is a promising area of research and that it is possible to predict CEFR levels with a considerable accuracy.
